model_annotation: The graph illustrates the training loss over iterations for several models, including Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and SepLLM variants with different configurations (n=64, H; n=64, H/T; n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis shows the loss value, scaled linearly from 2.4 to 3.4. All models begin with a high loss value near 3.3 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid initial decrease in loss. The Vanilla model (purple) shows the highest loss throughout the training process. StrmLLM (n=64) (blue) and SepLLM (n=64, H) (green) follow similar trends, with StrmLLM showing slightly higher loss than SepLLM (n=64, H) after the initial drop. SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red) and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue) show the lowest loss values, converging to a stable range around 2.5 by the end of training. The SepLLM (n=128) model demonstrates the most consistent and lowest loss performance across all iterations.
